title: Scaling Scientific Labor with Agentic Engineering and Lightcone Research
author: Cail Daley
venue: GDR CoPhy Tools WG, IAP Paris
description: Agentic engineering principles for cosmology, Lightcone Research, and two hands-on tutorials: Union2.1 supernovae and UNIONS Paper II B-modes.
footer: Cail Daley  GDR CoPhy Tools WG · IAP  2 Dec 2026

sections.title: Agentic engineering
sections.outline: Capabilities and falling token costs, new engineering constraints for astronomy, context and prompt caching, agent teams, searchable wikis, and simulation-based verification with its failure modes.

sections.title: Lightcone Research
sections.outline: Why high agent throughput needs structured provenance, the ASTRA specification and Lightcone stack, a live Lightcone Studio demonstration on UNIONS Paper II, and which scientific labor scales.

sections.title: Tutorial A: Union2.1
sections.outline: Build a Lightcone analysis from scratch on 580 Union2.1 Type Ia supernovae: setup across Claude Code, OpenCode and Codex, fit flat ΛCDM, verify Suzuki et al. (2012) against the cached PDF, and record systematic covariance as an ASTRA decision.

sections.title: Tutorial B: Paper II B-modes
sections.outline: Explore, click, and extend a published A&A cosmology analysis (UNIONS-3500 Paper II B-modes) in Lightcone Studio: clone the laptop branch, toggle decisions live, prompt a new universe, and edit a figure recipe.

sections.title: Backup
sections.outline: Cost versus intelligence benchmarks, harnesses as working environments, generated multi-agent workflows, HTML review reports, and optional Lightcone Lab setup in JupyterLab.
